title: Hydraulic Power Unit

introduction.definition: A hydraulic power unit (HPU) supplies pressurised oil to hydraulic actuators. An electric motor drives a pump (gear, vane or piston) through a bell housing and coupling. The pump draws oil from the reservoir and delivers it through a manifold with a pressure relief valve and check valve. Return oil passes through a filter and cooler back to the tank.
applications: Presses, injection moulding and machine tools
key_points: Pump makes flow; the load makes pressure
Cleanliness (ISO 4406) is the key to reliability
Reservoir typically sized ~ 3–5 × pump flow per minute (industrial rule of thumb)
introduction.summary: A hydraulic power unit (HPU) supplies pressurised oil to hydraulic actuators. A motor drives a pump that draws oil from the reservoir; a relief valve limits pressure, filters keep the oil clean, a cooler removes heat, and the oil returns to the tank after doing work.

pressure.description: Blue = suction (slightly below atmospheric at the pump inlet — keep it short and generous). Red = pressure line, limited by the relief valve setting (system pressure is set by the load; the relief valve caps it). Green-blue = return line, a few bar back-pressure through the return filter.

foundation: Mount on a level, rigid base with access for filters, gauges and fill; drip tray/bund under the reservoir.
alignment: Align motor and pump with the bell housing and coupling; mount cylinders so the rod is not side-loaded (use spherical bearings/clevises).
piping: Clean (pickled/flushed) pipework sized for velocity (typical guide: suction ≲ 1.2 m/s, pressure 3–6 m/s, return ≲ 3 m/s); hoses not twisted or rubbing; correct fittings for pressure.
Fit pressure gauges/test points, and relief protection on every pressure source.
commissioning: Fill through a filter with the specified oil; flush the system to the target cleanliness (ISO 4406 code).
Bleed air; start with relief valves backed off, then set pressures; check for leaks, temperatures and noise.

routine.task: Check oil level, temperature and filter indicators.

periodic.task: Oil sample (ISO 4406 particle count, water, acidity).

overhaul.task: Replace filters, breather and seals; check pump wear (case drain flow for piston pumps).

lubrication: Motor bearings greased; hydraulic oil changed by condition.

causes: Cooler fouled, relief valve blowing, internal leakage
remedies: Clean cooler; check relief setting and pump wear

causes: Blocked strainer, low oil level, cold oil
remedies: Clean strainer; correct level; warm up oil

safety: Release stored pressure (accumulators!) before opening any line; never search for leaks by hand — injection injury risk.

video_tutorials.title: Hydraulic Power Unit — Maintenance

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the Hydraulic Power Unit.
Check oil level, temperature and filter indicators.
Oil sample (ISO 4406 particle count, water, acidity).
Replace filters, breather and seals; check pump wear (case drain flow for piston pumps).
Watch for overheating: oil > ~ 60 °c. Common cause: cooler fouled, relief valve blowing, internal leakage.
Watch for pump cavitation: noise, erosion, low output. Common cause: blocked strainer, low oil level, cold oil.
Watch for contamination: valve sticking, wear. Common cause: poor filtration, dirty breather.
Record every inspection so trends — vibration, temperature, leakage and performance — can be compared over time.
